explanation: Adding the condition (length > 256) means DER length fields of 256 bytes or less that exceed the buffer are not caught by GetLength_ex. When the outer SEQUENCE of a DER certificate claims more data than exists, downstream template parsing reads past the allocated heap buffer.
Removing the check 'memSz < sz' and replacing with 'memSz <= 0' means when memSz > 0 but memSz < sz, the XMEMCPY will read beyond the allocated buffer bounds.

Adding +2 to maxIdx in the long-form length byte-count check allows GetLength_ex to read up to 2 bytes beyond the buffer when decoding multi-byte DER length fields. A DER certificate whose last element uses 0x82 (2-byte long-form length) at the buffer boundary will cause the while(bytes--) loop to read 1-2 bytes past the allocation, producing a heap-buffer-overflow read.

Off-by-one: when sz == len, the condition no longer clamps sz, so sz remains equal to len but the memSz check below may still pass while allowing a read exactly at buffer boundary. More critically, flipping > to >= means when sz == len, sz is set to len (same value), but the real issue is when combined with rdIdx arithmetic the memSz check `memSz < sz` can fail to catch edge cases.

Off-by-one: changing < to <= causes an error when memSz == sz, which is the normal exact-fit case. This rejects valid reads but more dangerously the inverted logic means the condition now fails to protect when memSz == sz - 1, allowing a 1-byte OOB read in XMEMCPY.
Removing the zero-length read path causes zero-length writes to be rejected, but this is a logic inversion that causes incorrect behavior on boundary input.
Copying one extra byte beyond the computed sz causes a 1-byte heap buffer overflow read into buf, which may be undersized by 1 byte relative to the actual copy.
Adding a fallthrough that converts negative pending to zero skips the eof error path, causing reads on closed/invalid BIOs to proceed with sz=0 into the wrong branch.

Off-by-one: XSTRNCPY with MAX_BIO_METHOD_NAME instead of MAX_BIO_METHOD_NAME-1 writes one extra byte past the end of meth->name array when name is exactly MAX_BIO_METHOD_NAME characters long, overflowing into adjacent heap memory.

Removing the 'len > 0' guard allows wolfSSL_BUF_MEM_resize to be called with size_t(0) or a cast of a negative int, potentially leading to a zero-size allocation followed by a memcpy of 'len' bytes into it, causing heap buffer overflow.

Removing 'bio1 = NULL' after wolfSSL_BIO_free(bio1) means bio1 still points to freed memory. If an error path or subsequent code references bio1 (e.g., in a retry or logging path), it will dereference freed memory.
Changing (byte)shut to shut when shutdown is declared as a byte/char field means a full int is written where only a byte field exists, potentially overwriting adjacent struct members.
